title: Gaussian Blending Unit: An Edge GPU Plug-in for Real-Time Gaussian-Based Rendering in AR/VR
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting on edge GPUs (e.g., Jetson Orin NX) achieves only 7-17 FPS for AR/VR rendering, far below the 60+ FPS threshold for immersive experiences, because the Gaussian Blending Stage—computing each Gaussian's contribution at every pixel—dominates compute time and is poorly suited to conventional GPU pipelines.
motivation: AR/VR applications demand real-time photorealistic rendering on resource-constrained edge devices, and 3D Gaussian Splatting is the leading technique for rendering quality and efficiency, but its pixel-blending stage is the primary bottleneck on edge hardware.
method: GBU is a hardware module for edge GPUs that accelerates the Gaussian Blending Stage—the calculation of each Gaussian blob's contribution to every pixel. It processes pixels row by row, left to right, using a two-step coordinate transformation that reuses calculation values between adjacent pixels (cutting work by up to 5.5×) and skips Gaussians that contribute minimally (saving up to 93% per pixel). A Gaussian Reuse Cache reduces memory accesses by 44.9%, and a dedicated rendering engine balances workload across Gaussians.
key_novelty: Intra-row sequential shading (IRSS) processes each row left to right, where a two-step coordinate transformation exploits adjacent pixels' similarity to simultaneously reuse intermediate calculations and skip Gaussians that contribute minimally—both optimizations in one unified pass.
contributions: Comprehensive bottleneck analysis identifying the Gaussian Blending Stage as the primary performance limiter for 3D Gaussian Splatting on edge GPUs
IRSS dataflow with two-step coordinate transformation enabling 5.5x intermediate value sharing and 93% per-pixel computation reduction via early culling
Dedicated rendering engine balancing workload across rows by aggregating multi-Gaussian computations
Gaussian Reuse Cache reducing off-chip memory accesses by 44.9% with a 1.14x additional speedup; 1.72x GPU-software speedup and real-time performance via the GBU plug-in

metrics.speedup: 1.72x on GPU with IRSS dataflow alone; real-time (60+ FPS) achieved with full GBU plug-in on Jetson Orin NX (vs. 7-17 FPS baseline)
metrics.other: off-chip memory access reduced by 44.9%; per-pixel computation reduced by up to 93%

baselines: Jetson Orin NX Edge GPU baseline (3DGS native implementation)
primary_theme: edge GPU plug-in for real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering
